name: Opal Efficiency Case Study — Mechanical/Semantic/Behavioral audit of the comp-tool framework
description: Andrew-direct charter 2026-07-23 (verbatim in PRD s.0): the comp tools exist to rapidly inject extremely high-signal context fluidly; audit the framework on three layers -- MECHANICAL (tools get their data fast + reliably), SEMANTIC (the right tool is findable for the query), BEHAVIORAL (agents actually reach for the tools) -- using the most convoluted Opal projects/scenarios as the case-study base, to identify where the holistic framework is lacking most. Bar: a light query against standing Opal context should make the intent AND the completing context immediately obvious; process architecture (CLAUDE.md/XXX.md/prompts) is good pretext, the missing layer is true state+dependency understanding, which the tools must solve. Phase 0 = programmatic audit of every compiler-tools-log row (last 3 months).
phase: Phase 0 COMPLETE 2026-07-23: .tools/msbeff-log-audit.py landed + first pass over 21,775 rows (denominators printed, both schema eras, nothing dropped). Headline findings: 8.5% FAIL concentrated on workhorses (pipescript 23%, blast 22%) and record-keeping tools (registry/tooltip 44%); 129 referenced tool names vs 83 registered (~46 phantom refs incl. retired tools still cited); comp-which <0.9% of flow; ~55% of volume is auto-invoked (surface-check/pulse) not chosen; 61.6% of rows outside TO context. Next: Phase 1 (FAIL taxonomy + AUTO-vs-CHOSEN classifier), Phase 2 (convoluted-scenario case studies, MDPF arc first), Phase 3 (ranked weakest cells -> expansion items).
